Has definitely become more and more PvP from what it was. If you like that sort of game then go for it. Otherwise, find something else because this is just another battle royale disaster. Extraction and spawn campers are starting to pop up more and more too. It is practically impossible to fight medium to advanced ARC enemies without getting 3rd partied by a person with a free kit.

Adding that this game has MAJOR ease of use issues as well. Menus are poorly organized. Inventory and stash lists have almost useless sorting options. The fact that when not the party leader you can't go look at maps and even just see what events are going on is annoying as hell too. How hard is it to allow party members to see more and just not see the Confirm button???

The quick use functionality is absolute garbage. First, I need to go to a clunky wheel method to select a quick use item to use AND then click another button to actually use it. Even though it shows the quick use in your HUD I have to go into it to use it again. Unless of course if I just used one of those items and then it will require me to put it away, Just poorly designed and could work so much better.

Barely any explanation on how trials actually work and the skill tree descriptions are so vague you aren't even sure that what you are picking is even useless which sucks even more when you can't change after you select one.

The fact that you can spend the time to create a custom loadout (which is dumb that you cannot create and save loadouts to use instead of having to build from scratch each time) and then get spawned into a round that is almost 50% over already is just awful. You want to throw spawns in mid-round? Make them free loadouts only or don't have them at all.

Starting to see more and more bugs where bots can shoot through walls, trees, cars, etc. but you can't. Had one today where a wasp first shot us through a wall and then phased through it itself.

The maps are almost too cluttered as half the time your raider will easily run over medium objects or steps and then not able to get over small ones. Not to mention the fact he won't climb on certain things but then on random others.

Was fun for awhile but all in all you start to realize it was just another 3rd-person extraction shooter jammed out by lazy developers and has the same old crappy design and playability issues.

I didn’t expect to enjoy this game as much as I do. It’s wild, unpredictable, and somehow even fun when everything goes wrong. The voice chat is pure chaos in the best way.. you never know if the next person you meet will help you out or rob you blind while laughing. That uncertainty is honestly a huge part of the charm.

Under the hood, the systems are genuinely strong. Upgrading your stash with in-game currency, building out your gear, watching your hideout slowly improve.. it all feels rewarding and well thought out. Even the lore seeps in naturally over time, and the atmosphere absolutely nails that broken-world, barely-holding-together vibe.

What really stands out is how different this feels from the usual hardcore PvP grind. When encounters turn into tense standoffs, weird social moments, or uneasy cooperation, the game is at its best. There’s something uniquely cinematic about it that you don’t get from pure sweat-fest shooters.

It’s also reassuring to see the devs actively leaning into that vision. The aggression rating system that nudges players into lobbies with similarly aggressive (or more laid-back) players feels like a smart way to preserve the game’s identity without forcing a single playstyle. If they keep refining that balance and letting the social chaos breathe, this game has real potential to stand apart instead of becoming just another Tarkov clone.

Straight up, this game is easily in top 3 games of all time for me. Everything in this game just feels so good - even losing everything. It's punishing and forgiving, it's challenging yet easy to grab a hold of, the highs are high and the lows are low.

Some people wish this was a PvE only game. That, to me, makes zero sense. The game has a very heavy focal point on PvE, and I think a solid balance of PvE and PvP in both solos and squads.

Other complaints I have seen point out the monetization scheme of this game, that being, paying $20 for a skin in a $40 base game. Yes, that is way to steep. Is that the end of the world? No. People are down-voting the entire game for this aspect - which is just WILD to me. The skins are optional, they are cosmetics, they make no difference to gameplay. This system should be reformed, but does not call for a down vote just because of this. However, I hope future raider decks will somewhat remedy this issue, as to give players at least a decent selection of cosmetic rewards for playing the game.

But yeah, game is 100% a great buy. I give it a 9.5/10.

[h1]Initial review[/h1]
I was ready to ask for a refund after my first 3 games, in which I got killed from out of nowhere in the first minute. Peak unfun.

But then I went for a fourth run, and I managed to extract. I didn't have this sense of excitement since I  put €20 on black after a 6 red streak on online roulette. After that, I've managed to extract 80% of the time. The community is so great, and every run is a story on its own. You will meet both very kind people who just want to coexist (the majority), or silent killers who do not care if you only have a pickaxe on you. This emotional rollercoaster is what keeps this game so fresh, as you never know who to trust.

The music is amazing, the world looks fantastic, the gameplay feels REALLY good, and the ambiance is unmatched. I've been playing solo until today, where I did some duo runs with a colleague -- and we had a blast. There is even a (beta) feature that changes your voice to male or female... imagine how much you can exploit this << Nobody kills a girl, right? >>

The game truly is in a bad position right now and they really need to add something ASAP. I used to defend the lack of updates since the game just came out, but now it has been a too long.

I've done it all at this point, twice. I'm not even motivated upgrading my crafting stations to level 2. My friends are tired of it. I just submitted a refund, and I know why this game didn't stick with me..

I enjoy extraction shooters. If it wasn't for Warzone Cash Extraction mode or The Division extraction mode, I wouldn't be here. The funny thing is, this is all about loot n' shoot, so why am I not enjoying it? It's because that's the only thing to do in the game, whereas in The Division and Warzone, there are other game modes to fulfil my interests. I gave this game a good 3 hours, and I would have liked to given it more, but I didn't want to risk losing my refund.

I don't blame the game. They advertise it as shown and describe it well enough on their Steam page. I was being hopeful and thought of giving it a go. Sadly, it didn't live up to my expectations. At the end of the day, it's just a boring looter shooter in an empty world. I would only see myself returning if they added more PVE elements, big events happening throughout the world, quests that are actually meaningful and not about collecting sh1t. Oh, and 3rd person really takes out the fun. I do believe they dropped the ball on that part.

All n' all, it's a meh shooter game. The price is great, and if you're into this then buy it, however, If you're looking for bit more oomph then give this game a pass.
